parts.title: The worst present ever
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
On my twelfth birthday, my aunt gave me a pair of pink socks. I was not pleased. I had hoped for a bicycle, and I had told everybody in my family about it for months. Instead, I got socks, a card with a cat on it and a hug that lasted too long.

My mother saw my face and whispered, "Say thank you." I did, but I did not smile. Later, I put the socks at the back of a drawer and forgot about them.

A year later, my aunt became ill and spent a long time in hospital. When I visited her, she was in bed, knitting something. She told me that she had made those socks herself, and that she had used the last of her wool. I felt terrible. I went home and found them at once.

I wore them the next day, even though it was summer, and I showed her. She laughed until she cried. Today, I am thirty, and those socks are still in my drawer, although they are too small. I would not give them away for any bicycle in the world.

questions.prompt: What had the writer hoped for?
questions.explanation: She had hoped for a bicycle.

questions.prompt: What did the mother do?
questions.explanation: She whispered "Say thank you."

questions.prompt: What did the writer learn about the socks?
options: They were a present from her mother
questions.explanation: Her aunt had made the socks herself.

questions.prompt: How did she feel then?
questions.explanation: She felt terrible.

questions.prompt: What does she think of the socks now?
questions.explanation: She would not give them away for any bicycle.

parts.title: Birthdays around the world
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
People celebrate birthdays in very different ways. [1] In many countries, the main thing is to have a cake with candles, and the birthday child makes a wish before blowing them out.

In some places, there are special customs. [2] For example, in Denmark, the flag is put outside the window on the morning of a birthday.

In Mexico, children often have a piñata. [3] When it breaks, sweets and small toys fall out, and everyone runs to pick them up.

In some parts of China, people eat long noodles on their birthday. [4] They believe that the longer the noodles, the longer the person will live.

Whatever the tradition, the idea is the same. [5] A birthday is a day when family and friends show someone that they are special.
sentences: Cakes are cheaper in supermarkets than in bakeries.
The noodles must not be cut, so people try to eat them in one go.
The way of celebrating may change, but the day is always important.
Some of them may surprise visitors.
Children there often wake up to find presents beside their beds.
It is a paper animal filled with treats, and the children hit it with a stick.
Some customs are known all over the world.
Some families keep the candles to use again next year.

gaps.explanation: Some customs are known all over the world, for example the cake with candles in the next sentence.
Some customs may surprise visitors; the next sentence gives Denmark as an example.
The piñata is a paper animal with treats; the next sentence says that when it breaks, sweets fall out.
The noodles must not be cut; the next sentence gives the belief.
"Whatever the tradition, the idea is the same": the way of celebrating changes, but the day is always important.

We are going to have pizza and games [3] the garden. My brother has promised to play music, [4] he usually forgets. Please let me know [5] you can come by Wednesday. Do not bring a present, because I have everything I [6]. See you soon! Talia

parts.title: Choosing a gift
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Choosing the right gift can be quite difficult. Some people spend weeks thinking [1] what to buy. A good tip is to listen carefully to your friends during the year. They often mention things they would like [2] have. Another idea is to give something you have made yourself. A handmade present shows that you took the trouble [3] think about the person. If you are short of money, [4] not give your time? You could offer to cook a meal or to help with the garden. Remember that it is not the price that matters, [5] the thought behind the gift. And do not forget to wrap it nicely, because a pretty package makes any present seem [6] special.

gaps.explanation: Would like is followed by to and the verb have.
The phrase take the trouble is followed by to and a verb.
Why not followed by a verb is used to make a suggestion.
Not the price but the thought.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: I want to buy a scarf for Gran’s birthday. She loves red, I think.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: She wore a red one last winter, and it’s getting old, so she may like something new. Green matches her coat, but she already has two green ones.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: What do you suggest, then?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Her eyes are blue, and the lady in the shop told me that blue goes well with grey hair. Do you want me to come with you?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Yes, please. It’s a big surprise for her, so let’s be quick.

question.explanation: Red was last year’s scarf and she already has two green ones; the shop lady said that the colour of her eyes suits grey hair.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: When’s your birthday, Pete? I need to buy a card.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: The fourth of March. No, wait, that’s my brother’s. Mine is the fourteenth of March. I’m turning forty this year, the big four-oh, which is why my wife is planning something.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Forty! You don’t look it.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Thanks. She wants a party in the garden, but it will be cold, so I’m not sure.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: I’ll put the date in my diary. The fourteenth.

question.explanation: He first says the fourth, but that is his brother’s birthday, and he corrects himself to the fourteenth of March.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Hi Sally, it’s Max. I’ve counted everything for the party. Food is no problem, my mum has made enough sandwiches and cakes for thirty people, so we’ll have plenty. And I don’t need to worry about music, because Dan is bringing his speakers and a long list of songs. But there are only ten chairs for twenty guests, and some of them are in the garage with a broken leg. Please ask your neighbours to lend us some. Call me back when you can. Thanks.

question.explanation: He has plenty of food and Dan brings the music, but there are only ten chairs for twenty guests.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Here’s the paper and the scissors. Do you need anything else for the wrapping?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: I already have paper, thanks, and my scissors are in my bag. My problem is that the corners won’t stay down, and my hands aren’t big enough.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Do you want some glue?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: It would stain the paper. You’ve got the tape in the drawer, haven’t you? The clear one.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Of course. Here you are. Be careful, it’s the last piece of the roll.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Don’t worry, I only need a little.

question.prompt: What does the woman ask for?
question.explanation: She does not need paper or scissors; the corners will not stay down, so she asks for the clear tape in the drawer.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Hi Dad, it’s Ruby. I’m at the card shop in the high street. I’m not in a rush because of the party, it starts at six and I have more than an hour. And the card isn’t expensive, it only costs three pounds, so I have enough money. But the lady has just told me that the shop closes in fifteen minutes. So I’ll choose one quickly, pay, and come straight home. See you soon. Please don’t start without me!

question.explanation: The party is far away and the card is cheap; the shop closes in fifteen minutes.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: What did you get for your birthday, Leo? A bicycle?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: I wanted one. Dad said maybe next year, when I’m taller. And Auntie Rose offered to buy me a guitar, but I can’t play a note. In the end I got a football, the same one as my friend Max’s, with a gold star on it.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Great. Are you going to try it today?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Yes, after lunch, in the park.

question.explanation: He wanted a bicycle but must wait, and he cannot play a guitar; he got a football like Max’s.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Hello Uncle Tom, it’s Josh. It’s about my birthday. Mum said we could have the party at home, but it’s too small for fifteen people. So I suggest the sports centre. I know it’s not near, we need to go there by bus. It isn’t quiet either, because people are swimming and playing basketball at the same time. But it’s really cheap, the best price, only forty pounds for two hours, and there is a room with tables. Please tell me what you think. Bye.

question.prompt: Why does he suggest the sports centre?
question.explanation: The centre is far away and noisy, but the price is very good, forty pounds for two hours.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Look what Gran gave me, a book of poems with my name inside.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: I thought you wanted a phone.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: I did, I told Mum at Christmas. But I like this more. Gran wrote a message in the front, and it’s all about me. It’s quite big, but I don’t care.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: That’s lovely. She’s the best.

turns.speaker: a

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Happy birthday, son. What would you like? Some money? A new phone?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: I already have a phone, and I’m saving for a game, so I don’t need money. What I’d really like is to go fishing with you, like we used to, just the two of us.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: I’d love to spend time with you, but I’m very busy at the moment, with the new job.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: I know, but maybe on Sunday?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: You’re right. Let’s go on Sunday morning.

question.explanation: The boy refuses the phone and the money; he wants to spend a morning fishing with his father.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Hello, I ordered a birthday cake for Saturday. There’s nothing wrong with it, I saw the picture and it looks wonderful. The problem is that you said ten in the morning, but the party begins at noon, and I’m out until half past eleven. Could it come at one instead?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Of course. One o’clock is fine. We can change the time without any extra charge. The driver will call you before he arrives, so please keep your phone on.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Perfect, thank you so much. The cake looks great in the photo, and my daughter is going to love it. I’ll recommend your bakery to all my friends.

question.explanation: She already has the cake and is happy with it; she needs it later, at one o’clock.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Have you written the invitations?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Twenty! It’s too many. Mum says the house is small. I thought of cancelling the party, but I don’t want to disappoint anyone. So I’ll cut the list to ten, close friends only.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Do you want me to help you?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Yes, please. Then I’ll tell everybody by message, not by phone, it’s faster.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Make a list on paper first, and be careful to include Anna, because she was angry last year when you forgot her.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: I won’t forget her again, don’t worry.

parts.title: A message from a party organiser
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: organiser
turns.text: Hello, this is Keren from Sunny Parties. I am calling about the birthday party for your daughter. First, the date. You asked for the second of June, but the room is taken, so I have booked it for the twenty-second of June, a Saturday. The room is free from two o’clock in the afternoon. Another party has it in the morning until twelve, and then we clean. You must finish by five o’clock, because the cleaners arrive at half past five. Now the price. The room alone is fifty pounds, and the food and drinks are an extra thirty. But we have a package, and with the food and drinks and everything else the price is ninety pounds. The package includes a clown for an hour. Some customers prefer a magician, but he costs extra, forty pounds, and the clown is already included. Next, the guests. The room is big, but the fire rules say that the maximum is twenty-five children. Last time you invited thirty, which is too many, so please keep to twenty-five. Parents who stay are not counted, but they must sit at the back, where the tables are. Please also tell the families that there is no parking at the front, so the car park behind the library is better. Finally, the extras. A photographer costs thirty pounds for the afternoon. A cake costs fifteen pounds, but you said you would bring your own, so we don’t need to arrange it. Call me back if you want the photographer, because I need to book one a week before. Thank you, and I look forward to hearing from you. Have a lovely week, and say hello to your daughter from all of us at Sunny Parties.

gaps.prompt: The party will take place on the ___ of June
gaps.explanation: She wanted the second of June, but the room is taken, so it is on the twenty-second.

gaps.prompt: The room must be empty by ___ o'clock
gaps.explanation: The cleaners come at half past five, and the previous party ends at twelve; the family must finish by five.

gaps.prompt: The package with food and drinks costs ___ pounds
gaps.explanation: The room alone is fifty and the food extra thirty, but the whole package is ninety.

gaps.prompt: The package gives the children a ___ for an hour
gaps.explanation: The magician is an extra at forty pounds; the clown is included.

gaps.prompt: The room can hold no more than ___ children
gaps.explanation: Last time there were thirty, which was too many; the maximum is twenty-five.

gaps.prompt: A photographer for the afternoon costs ___ pounds
gaps.explanation: The cake costs fifteen and they bring their own; the photographer costs thirty.

parts.title: An interview with a cake maker
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Lyra, you make cakes for a living. What happened with your first cake?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Ha, it was a disaster. I was twelve, and I wanted a birthday cake for my dad. It wasn’t perfect and it didn’t burn, the oven was fine. But I didn’t wait for it to cool, so when I cut it, it fell apart in my hands. We ate it with spoons, and my dad said it was the best one he’d ever eaten.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What was the strangest cake you’ve made?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: A man asked for a football pitch, which is quite common, and another for a car, but the strangest was a washing machine. It had a door made of sugar glass and little clothes inside, made of fondant, turning round in blue jelly water. The customer was a laundry owner, so it was a perfect present. He cried when he saw it, and he took photographs for an hour before he cut it.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How long does a big cake take?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: People think two hours, because that’s the time for a normal cake, and nobody takes two weeks for one. For a wedding cake, I need about two days. One day for the sponge and the filling, and another for the decoration. If I hurry, the cake shows it. Cakes need rest, like people. When I started I tried to finish in one night, and the result was terrible.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Why is your job hard sometimes?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: The clean-up takes hours, but I put music on and I don’t mind. Finding ingredients is easy, I have good suppliers. The hardest thing is that people want different things. The bride wants it simple, the mother wants five floors, and the groom wants chocolate. I have to make everybody happy, and sometimes I need three sketches before the family agrees.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Why do you eat toast after a day of tasting?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: After so much cake, I’m tired of sweet things. I don’t want another slice, or even soup. I want something dry and plain. A piece of toast with nothing on it is like a holiday for my mouth.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is your advice for people who bake at home?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Follow the recipe exactly, at least the first time. Don’t use lots of sugar, because the cake gets heavy, and don’t try to bake it fast with a hot oven, it will burn outside and stay raw inside. Weigh everything, be patient, and then you can start inventing.
